text.p: Shoney's Inc on Friday called its first quarter results disappointing and said it would be unrealistic to expect a positive earnings trend until same-store sales are positive on a sustained basis.

The company today reported first-quarter revenues of $363.3 million and a net loss of $13.8 million. The loss included special charges totalling $17.6 million ($11.2 million, net of tax) for impaired long-lived assets and to adjust carrying values of under-performing restaurants to estimated fair market value.

Revenues for the first quarter increased $63.1 million from the first quarter of 1996, mostly due to the acquisition of 176 Shoney's and 67 Captain D's restaurants from TPI Enterprises Inc effective Sept 9, 1996.
The revenue increase from the purchased restaurants and five restaurants opened in the quarter was offset somewhat by the closure of 50 under-performing Shoney's restaurants during the period.
Same-store sales for company-owned restaurants, including those acquired from TPI, fell 1.9 percent in the quarter, including a menu price increase of 2.0 percent.
Same-store sales for its Shoney's restaurants fell 2.9 percent, but rose 1.8 percent for its Captain D's restaurants.
The comparable-store sales for the first quarter include menu price increases of 2.5 percent for Shoney's restaurants and 1.1 percent for Captain D's.

"No one is more impatient than I that this turnaround is taking longer than expected," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer C. Stephen Lynn. "While I am confident that the company is headed in the right direction, I know we must speed up the delivery of results.

"We have made progress in our improvement plan. But the benefits from our multiple initiatives have come slower than we had hoped and expected. Our disappointing results for the first quarter are primarily the result of the decline in the comparable-store sales for our Shoney's restaurants...In addition, the Shoney's restaurants purchased from TPI had a substantial negative impact on the quarter as the transition and improvement in performance for those restaurants has taken longer than expected."
He added, "Until comparable-store sales are positive on a consistent and sustained basis, it's unrealistic to expect positive earnings trend."
